headline: Dell Technologies chief executive Michael Dell has said AI needs safeguards and controls and that government has a part in setting them.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a prominent business leader's general call for rules, with no specific proposal.
importance_line: Another major technology chief backing safeguards matters to the public as one more voice in the safety debate, then to lawmakers weighing rules, then to AI developers, but he names no law or rule.
summary: CNBC reports, as relayed by The Times of India, that Michael Dell, chief executive of the computer and server maker Dell Technologies, said in a CNBC interview that AI needs "safeguards and controls", comparing it to fire that "can heat your home" but "can also burn down your whole village", and that both companies and government have a part to play, though he named no specific law and said he is not a policymaker. In the same interview he said he expects AI to be "fine" for humanity and sees no AI bubble because there is "not enough supply" of computing power.
